title: Topological sort
summary: Order the tasks of a directed graph so that every arrow points forward. Start with tasks nothing depends on.

checkpoints.text: A directed graph with no cycles: think of 0 as "install", 1 and 2 as steps that need it, 4 as the last step. Each vertex is labelled with its in-degree: how many arrows point into it.
Only vertex 0 has in-degree 0, so only it can go first. It waits in the queue.
0 is output and its arrows are removed: 1's in-degree drops from 1 to 0, so 1 is ready.
3 waited until both 1 and 2 were done: its in-degree reached 0 only after the second arrow was removed.

0 1 2 3 4: every arrow points from earlier to later in this order. If a cycle existed, some vertex would never reach in-degree 0 and the output would come out short. This is Kahn's algorithm, O(V + E) with lists.
